summary: Hostile audit #14 — core/manager.py, the runtime hub

survived.title: async_initialize spawns loop-lifetime work with no teardown — after a config-entry reload the PREVIOUS manager writes its stale self.data over the live store
survived.mechanism: async_initialize (306) ends by spawning background work that outlives the config entry: the re-arm loop at 473-480 calls phase_runner.rearm_dock_phase_if_needed -> _spawn_dock_poller -> hass.async_create_task (jobs/phase_runner.py:98), and the external-run path arms hass.helpers async_call_later timers (learning/external_run.py:119 and :203, EXTERNAL_FINALIZE_GRACE_S=300s re-armed up to EXTERNAL_GRACE_MAX_RECHECKS=8, i.e. up to ~45 min of live timers). The manager exposes NO shutdown method (grep for 'def shutdown/async_shutdown/stop(' over core/manager.py, jobs/phase_runner.py, learning/external_run.py, live_refresh/ returns nothing) and registers nothing with the entry (grep 'async_on_unload' over those files returns nothing). async_unload_entry (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/__init__.py:465-546) removes listeners, trackers, services, panels and pops DATA_RUNTIME, but never cancels those tasks/timers. On reload, async_setup_entry builds a SECOND EufyVacuumManager (__init__.py:234) with its own EufyVacuumStorage/Store over the SAME STORAGE_KEY. The orphaned callbacks hold self._manager = the OLD manager and end in a full-dict write: learning/external_run.py:213 'await self._manager.async_save()' and jobs/phase_runner.py:856 'self._manager.hass.async_create_task(self._manager._async_save_logged())'. core/manager.py:803 async_save is a bare 'await self.storage.async_save(self.data)' — it writes the WHOLE root dict, so the old manager's pre-reload snapshot replaces everything the new manager has persisted since. No interleaving argument is needed: the stale write is a single scheduled callback, not a race across an await.
survived.user_impact: Every change persisted after a reload can be silently reverted. Concrete: user runs setup_add_vacuum, which saves the new vacuum then schedules a reload (services/setup.py:166); 2-5 minutes later the pre-reload manager's external-run grace timer fires, calls _finalize_external_run and async_save, and the store goes back to the snapshot without vacuum #2. The UI keeps showing the new vacuum (the live manager's in-memory dict) until the next HA restart, when it is gone — along with any rooms, profiles, themes, queue edits or job state saved in the same window. Same shape via Options-flow reload and the integration page Reload button. The orphaned charge/wait poller can also still call maybe_advance_phase and dispatch the next room, so a second manager and a dead one can both drive the same physical run.
survived.guards_checked: async_unload_entry (__init__.py:465-546) read in full — no manager teardown; _dock_poller_active (phase_runner.py:75) is per-PhaseRunner-instance so it cannot deduplicate across two manager instances; _still_ours() in the pollers only checks the OLD manager's own data, which still says status='started'; _external_grace_finalize's 'slot.get("status") != "external"' early return likewise reads the OLD dict; no EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP / async_listen_once anywhere in the integration; entry.async_on_unload is used only in __init__.py for the update listener and by the entity platforms, never by the manager.
confirmations: Confirmed from source. `grep -rn 'async_shutdown|def shutdown|async_on_unload|EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP'` over custom_components/ returns NO manager teardown — the only async_on_unload uses are the entry update listener (__init__.py:265) and the four platform callback unregisters. async_unload_entry (__init__.py:465-546) read in full: it removes listeners, services, panels, mapping/battery/error trackers and the AdapterCoordinator, and pops DATA_RUNTIME — it never cancels phase_runner poller tasks or the external_run async_call_later timers. Both orphan paths end in a whole-root-dict write against the SAME STORAGE_KEY: external_run.py:213 `await self._manager.async_save()` and phase_runner.py:856 `hass.async_create_task(self._manager._async_save_logged())`, and manager.py:803/808 are bare `await self.storage.async_save(self.data)`. async_setup_entry builds a second EufyVacuumManager (__init__.py:234) with its own Store over the same key. _still_ours / the `slot.get("status") != "external"` re-check both read the OLD manager's dict, so neither rescues. _dock_poller_active is per-PhaseRunner-instance and cannot dedupe across instances. The precondition (a live run or an open external capture at reload time) is ordinary, not exotic, and the orphaned poller can additionally dispatch the next phase to the device.

CONFIRMED end to end. async_unload_entry (__init__.py:465-546) read in full: it removes listeners, trackers, services, panels and pops DATA_RUNTIME, and never touches the manager's spawned work. grep for async_on_unload across the integration returns only __init__.py:265 (update listener) and the entity platforms — nothing registers a manager teardown; there is no shutdown/async_shutdown on EufyVacuumManager, PhaseRunner or ExternalRunManager, and no EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP hook. Both stale-write paths verified: learning/external_run.py:213 'await self._manager.async_save()' (reached after up to 8 x 300s re-arms via async_call_later at :203) and jobs/phase_runner.py:856 'hass.async_create_task(self._manager._async_save_logged())'. core/manager.py:803 async_save is a bare 'await self.storage.async_save(self.data)' — a whole-root-dict write, so the orphaned callback's OLD self.data replaces everything the NEW manager persisted since the reload. Nothing cancels the tasks: hass.async_create_task tasks are tracked at hass level and survive a config-entry unload. Concrete trigger: user calls setup_add_vacuum -> services/setup.py:162-167 saves the new vacuum then schedules async_reload; a second EufyVacuumManager is built at __init__.py:234 over the same STORAGE_KEY; 5 min later the pre-reload ExternalRunManager's grace timer fires, its 'slot.get("status") != "external"' check reads the OLD dict (still 'external', so it does not early-return), and async_save writes the pre-reload snapshot back — the new vacuum is gone on next restart. Severity holds at CRITICAL on the second path too: the old PhaseRunner's dock poller and the new one are both live for the same (vac, map, phase) — _dock_poller_active is per-PhaseRunner-instance and cannot dedupe across instances — so both can call maybe_advance_phase and dispatch the next room to the same physical robot.

survived.title: Room-history preload overwrites the persisted cache with {} whenever the rebuild throws, and marks the cache ready so it never retries
survived.mechanism: async_initialize seeds data['room_history'] from storage (line 316) and it is persisted by async_save like any other root key. _load_room_history_cache_sync (2206) wraps the ENTIRE rebuild — LearningHistoryStore construction, load_jobs_index, load_all_completed_jobs and every ingest — in one 'except Exception' (2252) that logs and falls through to 'return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})', i.e. an EMPTY dict on any failure (ensure_dirs/os.makedirs OSError on a read-only or relocated config dir, permission error, an ingest raising on a malformed record). async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional REPLACE — 'self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})[vacuum_key] = vacuum_history' (2275) — with no emptiness or sentinel check, and immediately adds the vacuum to _room_history_cache_ready (2276), so _ensure_room_history_cache (2195) will never schedule another rebuild for the life of the process. The preload is not opportunistic: sensor/__init__.py:227 fires it for every vacuum at platform setup on every startup, and rooms/room_crud.py:201/:268 and profiles/manager.py:689 discard the ready flag to force a rebuild after a room renumber/delete. The empty dict is then written to the store by the next unrelated async_save. Partial failure is worse than total: the try wraps the whole loop, so a throw on job file 7 of 30 keeps the first 6 and silently rolls every other room's last_cleaned_at back to an older value.
survived.user_impact: Every room's cleaning-history sensor and the card's last-cleaned/last-mopped chips read 'never cleaned' for the rest of the HA run, with nothing shown to the user (the only signal is a log line). The blank state is then persisted. It also silently weakens a destructive-action guard: setup/protection.py:63-72 derives the 'has_learning_data' protection reason from data['room_history'][vac][map] being non-empty, so a map that does have history drops a reason and can fall from 'high' (typed confirmation) to a lower protection level for map deletion.
survived.guards_checked: _ensure_room_history_cache (2195) — only guards against a concurrent/duplicate load, never against a failed one; _room_history_cache_loading is discarded in the finally (2286) but ready is set before it, so no retry; the 'or ["unknown"]' at 2279 only affects which map the update callback names, it does not detect the empty result; get_room_cleaning_history (2421) calls _ensure_room_history_cache but reads whatever is in data with no fallback to the pre-replace value; LearningHistoryStore.read_json (learning/history_store.py:157) swallows its own errors and returns None, so the outer except only fires for errors read_json does not cover — which is exactly the path-level ones.
confirmations: Mechanism confirmed: _load_room_history_cache_sync (manager.py:2206-2256) wraps LearningHistoryStore construction, load_jobs_index, load_all_completed_jobs and every ingest in ONE `except Exception` and falls through to `return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})` — {} on any throw. async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional replace at 2275 with no emptiness check and adds to _room_history_cache_ready at 2276, and _ensure_room_history_cache (2195-2204) early-returns forever after. room_history IS a persisted root key (core/storage.py saves the whole dict), so the empty value is written by the next async_save. setup/protection.py:63-72 does derive has_learning_data from data['room_history'][vac][map] being truthy, so the protection-reason claim holds. Severity corrected DOWN: I traced every raise site and read_json (history_store.py:157-177) swallows JSONDecodeError AND bare Exception, _safe_int/parse_timestamp guard the ingest, so the only realistic throw is a path-level OSError from ensure_dirs' four mkdir calls or list_job_files — a read-only/relocated/permission-broken config dir. That is narrow conditions, i.e. MEDIUM, not HIGH.

Mechanism CONFIRMED at manager.py:2206-2286. _load_room_history_cache_sync wraps the entire rebuild in one 'except Exception' (2252) and falls through to 'return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})' — an empty dict on any failure. async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional REPLACE at 2275 with no emptiness/sentinel check and adds the vacuum to _room_history_cache_ready at 2276, after which _ensure_room_history_cache (2198-2199) early-returns forever for this process. data['room_history'] is a persisted top-level key (seeded at 316, written by the whole-dict async_save), so the blank subtree is durable. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to MEDIUM: the trigger is narrower than HIGH implies. LearningHistoryStore.read_json swallows its own errors, so the outer except only fires on path-level failures (read-only/relocated config dir, permission error) or an ingest raising on a malformed record — none of which is a routine condition — and the ready flag is per-process, so a plain HA restart retries the rebuild. Wrong outcome when it does fire is real and silent (every room reads 'never cleaned' for the rest of the run, only a log line), which is MEDIUM, not data destruction.

survived.title: Startup re-seed of the bundled theme library resurrects themes the user deleted, and re-points default_theme_id
survived.mechanism: async_initialize constructs ThemeManager(self.data) at 347, whose __init__ (themes/manager.py:55-68) calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library (themes/preloaded.py:514). That seeder walks PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS and re-creates any spec id that is not currently in data['theme']['library'] (:525-542) — it has no record of user DELETIONS, only a 'don't clobber what exists' rule. The delete side has no matching guard: ThemeManager.delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) does a plain 'del theme["library"][theme_id]' with no source=='core' check, and the card renders the delete control for every preset except the current default (src/renderers/theme.js:511-518, wired at src/bindings/theme.js:1220). Sibling asymmetry: save/import stamp source='core'/user provenance and the seeder even backfills source='core' onto existing bundled entries (:534), so it KNOWS which entries are its own — it just never asks whether the user removed one on purpose. The seeder also re-stamps data['theme']['default_theme_id'] = 'theme_follow_ha' whenever the stored default is empty or names a missing theme (:544-546), which is exactly the state delete_theme leaves behind when the deleted theme was the default (:388-389).
survived.user_impact: A user who curates the theme library — deleting the bundled themes they do not want, with a confirm dialog implying it stuck — finds all of them back in the picker after the next HA restart, silently and with no error. If the deleted theme was the global default, the default is silently re-pointed at theme_follow_ha, changing the rendered theme for every vacuum that is not individually pinned.
survived.guards_checked: ensure_preloaded_theme_library's 'if theme_id in library: continue' (:527) protects EDITS to a bundled theme but not deletion; delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379) read in full — the only precondition is 'theme_id in library'; the card's delete button is suppressed only for state.defaultThemeId (src/renderers/theme.js:511), not for core-sourced presets; no tombstone/'deleted_preloaded' key exists anywhere in data['theme'] (the sub-tree seeded at themes/manager.py:64-67 is library/default_theme_id/vacuums only).
confirmations: Confirmed end to end. ThemeManager.__init__ (themes/manager.py:55-68) calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library, which at preloaded.py:525-542 re-creates any PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS id not currently in library (the `if theme_id in library: continue` at :527 only protects EDITS, and :534 backfills source='core' on survivors — so the seeder demonstrably knows which entries are its own). delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) read in full: its only precondition is `theme_id not in library`, then a plain `del theme['library'][theme_id]`, and :388-389 sets default_theme_id = None when the deleted theme was the default — exactly the state :544-546 re-stamps to 'theme_follow_ha'. No tombstone key exists anywhere in the theme sub-tree (only library/default_theme_id/vacuums are seeded). The card renders the delete control for every preset except state.defaultThemeId (src/renderers/theme.js:511-518) with no source check, and the path is service-backed (themes/services.py:202-206, SERVICE_DELETE_THEME).

CONFIRMED. themes/manager.py:55-68 calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library on EVERY ThemeManager construction (i.e. every async_initialize, every restart AND every reload), and themes/preloaded.py:514-546 re-creates any PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS id not currently in library — the only guard is 'if theme_id in library: continue' (:527), which protects edits, not deletions. There is no tombstone key anywhere in data['theme'] (the sub-tree is library/default_theme_id/vacuums only, manager.py:64-67). delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) read in full: its only precondition is 'theme_id in library' — no source=='core' check — and it sets default_theme_id=None when the deleted theme was the default (:388-389), which is precisely the state the seeder re-points to 'theme_follow_ha' at :544-546. Card side verified: src/renderers/theme.js:511-518 renders the delete control for every preset except state.defaultThemeId, so bundled themes are deletable from the UI. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to MEDIUM: no durable user data is destroyed (user themes are untouched; the resurrection ADDS entries), and the consequence is a presentation-layer surprise — deleted presets reappear, and the global default silently re-points. Recurring and silent, but cosmetic in effect, so MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

survived.title: The startup backfill and setup_progress migration hard-code Eufy vocabulary and structurally cannot consult the adapter
survived.mechanism: The backfill block (417-439) stamps _room.setdefault('floor_type', 'hardwood') and _room.setdefault('profile_name', 'vacuum_quick') into every stored room. rooms/room_defaults.py exists specifically to be THE single answer to 'what settings does a room start with', resolved from the brand's room_profiles.default_profile, and its module docstring enumerates the four hand-maintained copies of exactly these literals that it replaced; this block is a fifth copy that the refactor missed. It cannot be fixed in place by calling the adapter either: the whole block runs inside async_initialize, before register_brand_adapter (__init__.py:307), so _get_adapter_config would return None here. The same pattern sits in _migrate_setup_progress (551-561), which hard-codes completed_steps = ['add_vacuum','import_active_map','save_rooms'] — its own docstring calls them 'the three legacy Eufy steps' — rather than the adapter-declared list that the reader uses (setup/status.py:75 get_adapter_setup_steps). Today both shipped brands declare exactly those three ids (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:546, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:430), so nothing diverges yet.
survived.user_impact: No divergence on the two shipped brands today. A third brand whose room_profiles.default_profile is not 'vacuum_quick' would have any legacy room missing profile_name stamped with another brand's profile key at startup (get_room_profile falls back to the catalog default for an unknown name, so it degrades rather than crashes); a brand declaring a different setup-step vocabulary would have a pre-state-machine install stamped complete against step ids it does not declare, leaving its real first step showing as incomplete forever.
survived.guards_checked: profiles/room_profiles.py:243-261 normalize_floor_type coerces anything outside the allowed set back to 'hardwood', and get_room_profile (:264-291) falls back to the catalog default then DEFAULT_ROOM_PROFILE_NAME, so neither stamped value can crash a reader — this is a vocabulary/ownership defect, not a crash; setdefault means rooms written by current code (which always emit both fields via RoomConfig) are untouched, so only pre-release stored rooms are reachable; is_step_completed (setup/drift.py:171) is plain list membership, so extra stamped ids are inert.
confirmations: Confirmed by reading manager.py:417-439 and 528-561. The backfill stamps `_room.setdefault('floor_type','hardwood')` and `_room.setdefault('profile_name','vacuum_quick')`, and _migrate_setup_progress hard-codes completed_steps ['add_vacuum','import_active_map','save_rooms'] with its own docstring calling them 'the three legacy Eufy steps'. rooms/room_defaults.resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum is the extracted brand-resolved answer (save_managed_rooms uses it at room_crud.py:253-255, and build_managed_rooms makes new_room_defaults a REQUIRED arg precisely to stop this pattern), so this block is an unmigrated copy. The 'cannot consult the adapter here' point is also confirmed — the block runs before register_brand_adapter. Correctly scoped future_brand_only/LOW: both shipped adapters declare exactly those three step ids and normalize_floor_type/get_room_profile coerce unknown values, so nothing diverges today.

CONFIRMED as a vocabulary/ownership defect with no shipped-brand divergence. manager.py:429-430 stamps _room.setdefault('floor_type','hardwood') and _room.setdefault('profile_name','vacuum_quick'), and rooms/room_defaults.py's module docstring explicitly names itself THE single answer to 'what settings does a fresh room start with', enumerating the four hand-maintained copies it replaced — this backfill block is a fifth the refactor missed, and it is structurally unfixable in place because it runs inside async_initialize, before register_brand_adapter (__init__.py:307), so the adapter cannot be consulted. Verified the contrast: RoomMapManager.save_managed_rooms (rooms/room_crud.py:255) DOES route through resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum. _migrate_setup_progress (manager.py:551-561) hard-codes the same three Eufy step ids, and both shipped adapters declare exactly those, so nothing diverges today. Impact is future-brand-only and degrades rather than crashes (normalize_floor_type / get_room_profile both fall back), so LOW is correct.

survived.title: Room-update fan-out identifies "stale" entities by unique_id PREFIX, so a room edit on one vacuum permanently deletes a sibling vacuum's entities from the entity registry
survived.mechanism:
`_notify_rooms_updated(vacuum_entity_id, map_id)` (core/manager.py:622) carries the identity of the changed map as a TUPLE, but every entity-syncing subscriber throws that tuple away and re-derives ownership by string prefix. switch.py:71, number.py:101 and sensor/__init__.py:255 + :312 all compute `prefix = f"{vacuum_entity_id.replace('.', '_')}_{map_id}_"` and then classify every unique_id in their in-memory `entity_map` that `startswith(prefix)` and is not in `desired` as STALE — deleting it with `hass.async_create_task(stale.async_remove())` AND `_registry.async_remove(entity_id)` (switch.py:77-83).

The unique_id is built by `entity_helpers.make_room_unique_id` (entity_helpers.py:63-72) as `f"{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}"` where `vacuum_key = vacuum_entity_id.replace('.', '_')`. Both the vacuum key and the map id are variable-length, unquoted, and joined by the same `_` separator, so `<keyA>_<mapA>_` is a valid PREFIX of `<keyB>_...` whenever `keyB == keyA + "_" + mapA`.

That is exactly what Home Assistant produces for two identical robots: vacuum A = `vacuum.robovac` (key `vacuum_robovac`), vacuum B = `vacuum.robovac_2` (key `vacuum_robovac_2`). A's map "2" prefix is `vacuum_robovac_2_` — which every single one of B's room unique_ids begins with, on EVERY one of B's maps.

Nothing downstream re-checks ownership: `entity_map` is keyed by unique_id alone and stores no (vacuum, map) tuple; `_registry.async_get_entity_id("switch", DOMAIN, uid)` resolves the id without validating who owns it; and the room entities DO carry `_vacuum_entity_id` / `_map_id` attributes (room_entities.py) that the sweep never consults. The manager's fan-out then swallows nothing here because nothing raises — the deletion is the success path.

The sibling that got this right proves the shape: button.py:169 builds `f"{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_run_profile_"`, and the trailing literal segment makes a bleed impossible (B's map id would have to literally be `run_profile`). Only the four room-entity prefixes end on a bare `_`.
survived.user_impact: On any multi-vacuum install where one vacuum's entity_id is another's plus a numeric suffix (HA's own default for a second identical robot), the first room edit — toggling a room switch, applying a room profile, saving rooms, reordering the queue — on vacuum A's map "2" silently deletes ALL of vacuum B's room switches, room number entities, room-history sensors and rule-status sensors from the entity registry. Registry deletion is durable and takes the user's customizations with it: renamed entity_ids, custom names, icons and area assignments are gone, and every automation, script and dashboard card referencing those entity_ids breaks. No error is surfaced anywhere — the sweep logs nothing and `_notify_rooms_updated`'s try/except never fires because this is not an exception path. The entities reappear (as fresh, un-customized registry entries) only after a config-entry reload or HA restart.
survived.guards_checked: (1) `_notify_rooms_updated` core/manager.py:622-637 — passes vacuum_entity_id and map_id as separate kwargs; the loss of that separation is entirely on the consumer side, so the notifier offers no rescue. (2) `sort_room_items` (entity_helpers.py:75) — filters unconfigured rooms only; performs no vacuum/map scoping. (3) `desired` in every sweep is built exclusively from the notified vacuum/map's rooms, so a foreign entity can never be rescued by appearing in it. (4) `_registry.async_get_entity_id("switch", DOMAIN, uid)` — a pure unique_id lookup, no ownership assertion. (5) The `EufyVacuumRoomEntity` base (room_entities.py:41) stores `_vacuum_entity_id` and `_map_id` on each entity — a correct check is available and is not used. (6) button.py:166-169 — the only prefix builder with a trailing literal segment, and the only one immune; confirms the guard is absent rather than unnecessary. (7) config_flow.py:45-51 — single-instance domain, so this is not mitigated by per-vacuum config entries; __init__.py comments (line 579-586) confirm the design is explicitly "one entry manages many vacuums".
confirmations: Strongest finding in the set; confirmed line by line and I specifically tried to kill it on the scoping question. entity_map in switch.py:30 is built by iterating `manager.data['maps']` over ALL vacuums and ALL maps (switch.py:32-45) — it is ONE dict for the whole entry, not per-vacuum, so a foreign vacuum's unique_ids are genuinely present in the dict the sweep scans. The prefix is `f"{vacuum_entity_id.replace('.','_')}_{map_id}_"` at switch.py:71, number.py:101 and sensor/__init__.py:255/285/312/341, while make_room_unique_id (entity_helpers.py:63-72) emits `{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}` — both variable-length fields joined by the same separator, so vacuum.robovac + map '2' yields prefix `vacuum_robovac_2_`, which prefixes EVERY unique_id of vacuum.robovac_2 on every one of its maps. `desired` is built only from the notified vacuum/map, `entity_map` stores no ownership tuple, and `_registry.async_get_entity_id('switch', DOMAIN, uid)` performs no ownership check, so the foreign entities are removed from the entity registry (switch.py:77-83) — durable, taking renamed entity_ids/areas/customizations with it. The control case holds: button.py:166-169 is the only prefix builder ending in a literal segment ('..._run_profile_') and is the only one immune.

Mechanism CONFIRMED. entity_helpers.make_room_unique_id (entity_helpers.py:63-72) builds '{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}' with both variable-length fields joined by the same '_' and no quoting. switch.py:71-83 (and identically number.py:101-104, sensor/__init__.py:255/285/312/341, setup/delete.py:136) classifies stale purely by uid.startswith(f"{vac_key}_{map_id}_") and then does BOTH stale.async_remove() and _registry.async_remove(entity_id). Critically, entity_map is built across ALL vacuums (switch.py:32-45 iterates manager.data['maps'] for every vacuum), so a foreign vacuum's entities ARE in the sweep's search space; nothing re-checks ownership even though EufyVacuumRoomEntity carries _vacuum_entity_id/_map_id, and 'desired' is built only from the notified vacuum so it can never rescue them. Concrete case walked: vacuum.robovac (key vacuum_robovac) with a map id '2' yields prefix 'vacuum_robovac_2_', which every unique_id of vacuum.robovac_2 begins with on every one of its maps — and 'vacuum.robovac_2' is exactly what HA generates for a second identical robot. Verified the immune sibling: button.py:169 appends a trailing literal segment ('_run_profile_'), confirming the guard is absent rather than unnecessary. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to HIGH: it does destroy durable registry data (custom entity_ids, names, icons, area assignments) silently, but the trigger requires a specific naming coincidence — a multi-vacuum install where one entity_id is another's plus a separator and a matching map id — and the entities themselves are re-created on the next reload, so the loss is the customizations rather than the room configuration. HIGH rather than CRITICAL.

survived.title: async_preload_room_history_cache replaces the whole per-vacuum room_history subtree AFTER an executor await, silently discarding any room-history written during that await
survived.mechanism:
`async_preload_room_history_cache` (manager.py:2258) awaits `hass.async_add_executor_job(self._load_room_history_cache_sync, vacuum_key)` — a full disk read of the vacuum's completed-job files via `LearningHistoryStore.load_all_completed_jobs` — and then, at line 2275, does a WHOLESALE assignment:

    self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})[vacuum_key] = vacuum_history

This is a replace, not a merge. The executor result was snapshotted from disk before the await resolved, so any write to `self.data["room_history"][vacuum_key]` that landed on the loop DURING the await is destroyed.

A concrete writer exists on exactly that path: `async_finalize_learning_job` (manager.py:4618) awaits `learning.async_finalize_completed_job(...)` and then calls `_ingest_completed_job_into_room_history(vacuum_entity_id=..., completed_job=...)` with `_history_root` defaulting to None, which manager.py:2380-2385 resolves to `self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})` and mutates in place (`last_cleaned_at`, `last_vacuumed_at`, `last_mopped_at` per room), then fires `_notify_room_history_updated`. killed.title: Dock-phase re-arm runs INSIDE async_initialize (eager task start), so its brand lookups resolve before register_brand_adapter — Roborock gets Eufy phase timing and a battery read with no declared battery entity
killed.mechanism: The re-arm loop (473-480) is the last real statement of async_initialize and reaches hass.async_create_task(coro) at jobs/phase_runner.py:98. manifest.json requires HA >= 2025.6.0 (hacs.json), and since HA 2024.6 hass.async_create_task defaults to eager_start=True — the coroutine runs SYNCHRONOUSLY up to its first true suspension, i.e. inside async_initialize, not at the next loop yield. _run_charge_wait_phase awaits _run_charge_wait_phase_impl inline (phase_runner.py:604); that body is synchronous through get_active_job, the _still_ours check and get_battery_level, so on the common restart case 'battery already >= target' it goes straight into 'await self.maybe_advance_phase(...)' (phase_runner.py:645), which is also synchronous through _capture_finishing_phase_timing (a def, not async) and advance_active_job_phase, and then spawns _run_advanced_phase with another eager async_create_task (:192). _run_advanced_phase's FIRST statement is 'pt = self._manager._phase_timing(vacuum_entity_id)' (:515) and only then does it await asyncio.sleep. Meanwhile async_setup_entry has not returned from 'await manager.async_initialize()' (__init__.py:236), so load_stored_adapter_configs (:295) and register_brand_adapter (:307-314) have not run and hass.data[DOMAIN][DATA_RUNTIME] (:316) / DATA_LEARNING (:318) are unset. core/manager.py:4904 therefore resolves _get_adapter_config(...) to None and pt falls back to the in-core _PHASE_* defaults; the Roborock adapter declares confirm_seconds: 15 precisely because the core default of 45 is wrong for the S6 (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326). Same window: core/charging.py:50 loses the adapter's declared entities.battery and falls back to the vacuum entity's battery_level attribute (0 when absent). Note the ordering is safe WITHOUT eager start — there is no await between __init__.py:236 and :314 — so this defect exists only because the task starts eagerly.
killed.user_impact: After an HA restart during a charge_wait/wait phase, the first phase of the resumed run is driven with the wrong brand's watchdog timing for its entire duration (pt is read once). On Roborock the phase needs 45s of sustained cleaning-of-target to confirm instead of the declared 15s, so a normal short room never confirms inside the 90s verify window: the same room is re-dispatched up to max_attempts=3 times and the run can be left stalled ('recoverable via Cancel Run') even though the robot cleaned it. The adapter-less battery read can also report 0 and send the robot back to the dock for a charge it does not need.
killed.guards_checked: Traced every call between the re-arm and the adapter lookup for a suspension point — _still_ours, get_battery_level, _capture_finishing_phase_timing and advance_active_job_phase are all synchronous; _spawn_dock_poller's _dock_poller_active guard (phase_runner.py:85-88) prevents a double spawn but not early execution; _phase_timing (4896-4913) has no 'adapter not registered yet' branch, its try/except only covers int() coercion of declared values; get_adapter_config returning None is handled as 'brand declared nothing' rather than 'brand not loaded yet'; there is no await in async_setup_entry between line 236 and line 314 that would otherwise let the task run at a safe point.
killed_by: The eager-start observation is CORRECT — hacs.json pins HA >= 2025.6.0, hass.async_create_task defaults to eager_start=True, and I confirmed there is NO await in async_setup_entry between 'await manager.async_initialize()' (__init__.py:236) and register_brand_adapter (:307-314), so a task spawned from the re-arm loop does begin executing before the adapter exists. But BOTH claimed wrong outcomes are refuted by the code. (1) Phase timing: _run_advanced_phase's stale 'pt' is only used for settle_seconds, dock_settle_seconds and max_attempts — and adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326 declares settle 10 / dock_settle 45 / verify 90 / poll 5 / max_attempts 3, byte-identical to the core defaults at core/manager.py:74-99. The ONLY divergent key is confirm_seconds (15 vs 45), and _await_phase_started RE-READS its own 'pt = self._manager._phase_timing(vacuum_entity_id)' at phase_runner.py:889 — which runs after 'await asyncio.sleep(settle)', by which time async_setup_entry has completed and the adapter IS registered. So confirm_seconds is never taken from the stale read; there is no divergence on either shipped brand. The claimed stall is doubly refuted: _await_phase_started's terminal branch (phase_runner.py:960-965) returns 'cleaning_in_target > 0', a weak-confirm that explicitly treats a room finishing under confirm_seconds as confirmed rather than a no-show, so no re-dispatch and no stall. The interim return_to_base is a documented no-op on an already-docked robot ('a no-op if it is already docked + charging', phase_runner.py:669). The EXTENSION is that this is not only a crash window. `_dispatch_clean_payload` ends in `await hass.services.async_call(domain, name, data, blocking=True)` (dispatch/manager.py:84), so the event loop yields with the robot already commanded and NO active job on ANY map. `learning/external_run.py:75-96` documents its precondition as "Internal starts are blocked while a run is in progress, so a vacuum that is cleaning with NO dispatched job (status started/paused on any map) is an external run" and opens a `status="external"` capture slot when it sees `vacuum_state == "cleaning"` and `dispatched` is False. Separately, `_run_global_pre_calls` at 5005 permanently pushes global fan/water settings to the device (Roborock) before any record exists; if the dispatch then raises, the service handler re-raises as HomeAssistantError (services/job_control.py:151-154) and `async_save()` is skipped, so the device setting change is neither recorded nor restored.

The Roborock adapter declares settle 10 / dock_settle 45 / verify 90 / poll 5 / max_attempts 3 — byte-identical to the core defaults; the ONLY divergent key is confirm_seconds, and `_await_phase_started` re-reads `_phase_timing` itself at phase_runner.py:889, after the settle sleep, by which time the adapter IS registered. So the stale `pt` never supplies a value that differs on either shipped brand. The claimed stall is separately refuted by the weak-confirm at phase_runner.py:960-965 (`return cleaning_in_target > 0`). The battery claim fails too: with target defaulting to 100, a 0 read cannot satisfy `>= target`, so it enters the poll loop and self-corrects in 30s, and the interim return_to_base is documented as a no-op on a docked robot.
- A4-START-4: the ordering is exactly audit #13's WIRE-1 lead. Neither extension holds — the external-capture cross-talk needs the vacuum entity to flip to `cleaning` *inside* the blocking service call, which neither transport does, and the finder concedes it self-heals; and the Roborock pre-call is left changed on the success path too (by design), with the failure path surfacing a HomeAssistantError rather than failing silently.

CONFIRMED AND SEVERITY-CORRECT AT THE TOP:
- A5-FACADE-1 (CRITICAL) is the strongest finding in the set and I confirmed it by walking the full card path: `setup-save-rooms` binding -> `saveSetupRooms` -> `setup_save_rooms` -> `save_managed_rooms` -> unconditional `map_bucket["rooms"] = {}` -> `await async_save()`. The trap is sharper than the finder stated: the editor the user is saving from was populated by `setup_get_map_rooms`, which reads SAVED rooms, while the save rebuilds from the DISCOVERY cache — so the UI shows the rooms right up to the moment they are deleted. `reconcile_room` has the guard 60 lines above in the same class, with a comment naming this exact failure.
- A1-INIT-1 (CRITICAL) verified in full: no `async_on_unload`, no shutdown method, no `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP` anywhere; `async_save` is a bare whole-root-dict write; `_dock_poller_active` is per-PhaseRunner-instance so it cannot dedupe across two managers. The two-live-pollers-on-one-robot consequence is what keeps it at CRITICAL, not just the stale write.

DOWNGRADES:
- A2-CB-1 CRITICAL -> HIGH. The prefix bleed is real (I confirmed `entity_map` spans all vacuums, and that button.py:169 is immune only because it appends a trailing literal). But it needs a naming coincidence — vacuum B's entity_id equal to vacuum A's plus a separator and one of A's map ids — and the entities are re-created on reload, so what is destroyed is the customizations, not the room config.
- A1-INIT-2 and A1-INIT-3 HIGH -> MEDIUM; A3-SNAP-1 HIGH -> MEDIUM. All three are real, but none produces a wrong physical action or destroys user data: a blank history cache that retries on restart, a theme library that gains back entries, and a display badge during a sensor dropout on a brand where water is not settable anyway.
- A4-START-2, A4-START-3, A5-FACADE-3, A5-FACADE-4 MEDIUM -> LOW, all for the rubric's own reason: two are latent with no reachable caller (rebuild_map has zero production callers; the empty-zone dispatch is blocked by START-1's accidental gate), one is a messaging-only defect, and one is documented behaviour whose real content is sibling contract drift.

CLEAN AREAS (inspected, no finding): `_clear_orphaned_finalize_claims` (manager.py:484-508) does exactly what its docstring says and correctly clears unconditionally; the discovery flattening migration (443-446) is idempotent and shape-correct; the `carpet`/`carpet_type` compaction in the backfill (431-439) is correct and matches `get_floor_type_label`'s legacy handling; `_notify_*` fan-out try/except (622-654) correctly isolates subscribers; `zone_bounds` (4024-4034) and `scene_select`/`setting_entities` resolution are the right pattern and are what makes SNAP-1 and SNAP-4 stand out; `run_is_in_flight` / `dispatched_job_is_in_flight` (jobs/active_job.py:139-184) are a genuinely well-executed instance of centralising the question; `resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum` in `save_managed_rooms` is correctly brand-resolved (only the startup backfill missed it).
